title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: Ten documented Mizzou rituals, landmarks and recurring campus practices tied to the university’s history and student life.

cards.title: Answer “M-I-Z!” with “Z-O-U!”
cards.subtitle: Mizzou spirit chant
cards.notes: Join the call-and-response only when you hear it: answer “Z-O-U!” after “M-I-Z!” at games or around campus.
cards.short_summary: A concise call-and-response that signals Mizzou spirit.
cards.evidence_claim: Mizzou identifies “M-I-Z!” followed by “Z-O-U!” as its spirit chant.
cards.access_notes: The university says the chant is heard at games and around campus.

cards.title: Come Home for Mizzou Homecoming
cards.subtitle: Annual university-wide celebration
cards.notes: Look for official Homecoming programming and choose a public event that fits your visit, from the parade to service activities.
cards.short_summary: Mizzou traces its Homecoming tradition to a 1911 invitation to alumni.
cards.evidence_claim: Mizzou states its first Homecoming was held in 1911 after coach Chester Brewer invited alumni to return for the Missouri–Kansas game.
cards.access_notes: Programming is annual; consult official university event information for current dates and access.

cards.title: Watch the Homecoming Parade
cards.subtitle: Part of Mizzou Homecoming
cards.notes: Use official Homecoming details to find the current parade route and time, then watch from a designated public viewing area.
cards.short_summary: A parade is a documented component of Mizzou’s Homecoming celebration.
cards.evidence_claim: Mizzou lists a Homecoming parade among the events included in its city-wide Homecoming celebration.
cards.access_notes: Route, schedule and viewing access vary by year; verify with official Homecoming information.

cards.title: Recognize the Homecoming Blood Drive
cards.subtitle: Service element of Homecoming
cards.notes: If eligible and interested, consult the current official drive information before participating; otherwise learn how service fits into Homecoming.
cards.short_summary: Mizzou links its Homecoming celebration with an annual blood drive.
cards.evidence_claim: Mizzou identifies an annual blood drive as one of the good-cause efforts associated with Homecoming.
cards.access_notes: Participation is subject to current organizer, health and eligibility requirements.

cards.title: Run toward Jesse Hall at Tiger Walk
cards.subtitle: Francis Quadrangle to the Columns
cards.notes: Incoming students can follow Welcome Week guidance for the August run through the Columns toward Jesse Hall before classes begin.
cards.short_summary: A Welcome Week run marks the beginning of an incoming student’s Mizzou experience.
cards.evidence_claim: Mizzou says freshmen gather on Francis Quadrangle in August and sprint through the Columns toward Jesse Hall during Tiger Walk.
cards.access_notes: Held during Welcome Week before classes; follow current Welcome Week instructions.

cards.title: Reverse Tiger Walk at Senior Sendoff
cards.subtitle: May run through the Columns
cards.notes: Graduating seniors can check current commencement-period information for the May route, which reverses the Tiger Walk path.
cards.short_summary: Seniors symbolically leave campus by running the route in reverse.
cards.evidence_claim: Mizzou states that graduating seniors reverse the Tiger Walk route through the Columns at Senior Sendoff in May.
cards.access_notes: The university describes this as a May activity; verify current event details before attending.

cards.title: Paint the Rock M
cards.subtitle: Memorial Stadium landmark
cards.notes: Incoming students should use official Welcome Week directions if participating in the annual painting of the large stone M.
cards.short_summary: Each incoming class carries forward a Rock M painting tradition begun in 1927.
cards.evidence_claim: Mizzou says students created the Rock M in 1927 and that each incoming freshman class has continued the painting tradition.
cards.access_notes: This is a Welcome Week event; participate only through official event arrangements.

cards.title: Spot the Finals-Week Good-Luck Ritual
cards.subtitle: Bronze sculpture northeast of Jesse Hall
cards.notes: Find the David R. Francis sculpture northeast of Jesse Hall and note the long-running exam-luck legend surrounding its nose.
cards.short_summary: Students associate rubbing the sculpture’s nose with earning an A on the next exam.
cards.evidence_claim: Mizzou says students believe rubbing David R. Francis’ nose will earn an A on their next exam and notes the nose has been replaced three times.
cards.access_notes: The university locates the sculpture just northeast of Jesse Hall’s front entrance.

cards.title: Whisper Under Memorial Union’s Arches
cards.subtitle: Memorial Union
cards.notes: When passing under the arches, follow the customary quiet, respectful practice and remove or tip your hat in remembrance.
cards.short_summary: The arches carry a customary tribute to Mizzou students who died in military service.
cards.evidence_claim: Mizzou says it is customary to tip hats and speak in a whisper under Memorial Union’s arches as respect for fallen students.
cards.access_notes: The practice is associated with walking through Memorial Union’s arches.

cards.title: Find the Engineering Shamrock
cards.subtitle: Shamrock Plaza between Lafferre and Switzler Halls
cards.notes: Visit Shamrock Plaza to see the concrete shamrock, then consult engineering announcements for current E-Week programming.
cards.short_summary: The shamrock connects Mizzou engineers’ St. Patrick’s observance with E-Week.
cards.evidence_claim: Mizzou says College of Engineering students extend St. Patrick’s Day into Mizzou Engineers’ Week and identifies the shamrock medallion in Shamrock Plaza.
cards.access_notes: The medallion is located in Shamrock Plaza between Lafferre and Switzler Halls; event details vary.
